--- title: "Render a video to MP4" sidebarTitle: "Render" description: "Review the project, run its checks, render through an agent, the browser editor, or the CLI, and deliver the right file or link." --- Finish the same editable project through your agent, the browser editor, or the command line. The route can change; the quality gate does not. ## 1. Approve the project, not one good frame Watch the complete preview from the beginning. Check the message and sequence before spending time on small visual details. - Does the opening make the subject clear soon enough? - Does every scene add something? - Can text, captions, and product screens be read at delivery size? - Do narration, visuals, music, and sound effects arrive together? - Does the ending finish cleanly and make the next action clear? ## 2. Run the project checks Run the checks in the browser editor, ask your agent to run them, or use: ```bash npx hyperframes lint npx hyperframes check ``` `lint` catches composition-structure mistakes. `check` runs lint plus browser, runtime, layout, motion, and WCAG contrast verification. Checks cannot judge the story for you. Fix technical failures, then watch the project again if a fix changed what the viewer sees. ## 3. Render from where you are working All three paths render the same source. ### Ask the agent ```text Run the HyperFrames checks, fix any failures, and show me the final preview. When I approve it, render an MP4 to renders/final.mp4. ``` Use the agent when a failed check may require a source change or when you want one person to manage the complete finish. The `/hyperframes` skill waits for render approval after the final preview. ### Use the browser editor Open **Export**, choose the destination's format and size, and start the render. The Renders panel shows progress and keeps completed files available to download.
### Use the CLI ```bash npx hyperframes render --output renders/final.mp4 ``` Use the CLI for a direct local render, a script, CI, or a repeatable batch. The installed version remains authoritative: run `npx hyperframes render --help` for every available option. ## 4. Choose what the destination needs MP4 at the project's authored size is the normal delivery choice. Ask for another format or resolution only when the next tool or platform requires it. | Need | Start with | | ------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------- | | Watch, upload, or publish a normal video | MP4 | | Place a transparent overlay on the web | WebM with an alpha-compatible composition | | Continue in a professional editing tool | MOV, usually ProRes | | Deliver a specified high-resolution master | The matching 4K preset | Higher output resolution does not add detail to low-resolution media. A higher frame rate creates more frames; it does not improve motion authored for a lower cadence. Use [export in the browser editor](/studio/export) for its visible controls or the [rendering reference](/guides/rendering) for formats, Docker, batch output, and advanced CLI behavior. ## 5. Watch the rendered file Open the output itself instead of relying on the preview. - Watch the first and final seconds. - Check captions, cuts, and the most complex transition. - Listen for clipped narration, late sound effects, or an abrupt music ending. - Confirm duration, dimensions, format, and audio. - Use a filename that identifies the project and version. The preview proves the project can play. The exported file proves the delivery is correct. ## 6. Share the right form | The recipient needs | Send | | ------------------------------------- | --------------------------------- | | A video to watch or upload | The rendered MP4, WebM, or MOV | | A browser link to review the video | A video review link | | The ability to continue editing | The source project and its assets | To create a video review link, sign in, then run the following command from your project directory and choose who can open the link. ```bash npx hyperframes share ``` For scripts, pass an explicit audience as described in the [CLI sharing reference](/packages/cli#share). ### Update an existing published project `hyperframes publish` is deprecated for new projects. Existing published links still work. To update a project at its current URL, sign in and run `npx hyperframes publish --update `. A local video poster referenced with a relative path, such as `../shared/poster.png`, can be copied into the published project even when it lives outside the project directory, once you approve it (see below). Percent-encoded paths work too, such as `../shared/poster%20art.svg` for `poster art.svg` or `../shared/%E5%B0%81%E9%9D%A2.svg` for `封面.svg`. Local images outside the project referenced by an `` or `` element's `srcset` can be included the same way. Their size or pixel-density descriptors are preserved, and your source files stay unchanged. Only images, video, audio, fonts and CSS files are copied from outside the project. Any other outside file, such as a script, a Lottie `.json` or a `.pdf`, is left out with a warning naming it; move it into the project folder to include it. Nothing from outside the project folder is uploaded without your say. Before uploading, `publish` lists each such file, including files the project only links to, and asks whether to upload them. The answer defaults to no, which leaves them out. A yes is remembered for that project in your user config folder (`~/.hyperframes/outside-files.json`), never in the project, so the next publish asks only about new files. With `--yes`, or when nobody can answer the prompt, outside files are left out with a warning naming each one. Pass `--include-outside-files` to upload them without asking. Before sharing source, remove secrets and confirm that every included media file can be shared. Tell a reviewer whether you need feedback on story, visuals, timing, facts, or final approval. ## If the finish fails Keep the first exact error and run: ```bash npx hyperframes doctor npx hyperframes lint npx hyperframes check ``` Use [Troubleshooting](/help) for project and render failures, or [Browser editor troubleshooting](/help#in-the-preview-and-browser-editor) when the problem is in the editor or its render queue. ## Related topics - [Export and manage renders in the browser editor](/studio/export) - [Use advanced rendering options](/guides/rendering) - [Diagnose a project or render failure](/help) ## Share from the local Studio preview Open a project with `hyperframes preview`, then choose **Share** beside **Export**. Choose **Sign in** if prompted. You can also run `hyperframes auth login` in your terminal, then return to Studio. Sharing reconnects automatically after browser sign-in or when you return to the panel. Credentials stay in the local CLI process. If you switch accounts in the terminal, reload Studio or sign in from the panel before retrying. Choose the workspace and who can access the project, then choose **Create share link**. Studio finishes saving pending edits before it renders and uploads the project. The five free shared-project allowance is the same allowance used by Desktop and the CLI. The workspace meter comes from the server; retries of an existing registration do not need an extra slot. Before Studio creates a link, uploads a version, or changes who can open a review or whether its link is on, it asks you to confirm and names the review and who can open it. A project folder remembers its review in `.hyperframes/review.json`, so a folder someone sent you can arrive already linked to their review. If the confirmation names a review you didn't share, cancel. Project files are included only when you choose **Include editable project files**. The panel reports whether the last Studio upload included files or was video only. If attaching files fails, retry the upload or explicitly choose **Retry with video only**. When the video is ready, choose **Copy link**. Local edits do not automatically replace the shared video: **Update shared version** uploads the saved project to the same review page. Changes to access use a separate **Save access** action. **Turn link off** keeps the project and comments; updating the video keeps an off link off. Turning the link off does not free a shared-project slot. You can close the Share panel while sharing continues, but keep the local Studio server running. Reopen the panel to recover progress, or use **Refresh** after a connection problem. **Manage sharing** opens the web page for invites and owner settings. Existing published project URLs continue to open separately. The local sharing bridge is available only from the same-origin loopback Studio page. It does not expose CLI credentials or accept a different project path. As with local preview, open projects whose scripts you trust.
